rules:
# BOM sourcing rules (LibreBoard rev3)

You are sourcing parts for a KiCad PCB BOM. Input: a JSON list of part groups (one per manufacturer part
number, "mpn"), each with refs, value, footprint, description, the existing DigiKey number(s) ("dkpn"),
qty_per_board and a DNP flag. Plan for a build of 10 boards (needed qty = qty_per_board x 10).

Tools (MCP server "pcbparts"; load them first with ToolSearch, e.g.
`select:mcp__9d86586f-2121-426f-8ed6-a83a08c8fa40__digikey_get_part,mcp__9d86586f-2121-426f-8ed6-a83a08c8fa40__jlc_get_part,mcp__9d86586f-2121-426f-8ed6-a83a08c8fa40__jlc_search,mcp__9d86586f-2121-426f-8ed6-a83a08c8fa40__jlc_find_alternatives,mcp__9d86586f-2121-426f-8ed6-a83a08c8fa40__jlc_stock_check,mcp__9d86586f-2121-426f-8ed6-a83a08c8fa40__jlc_search_help`):
digikey_get_part, jlc_get_part, jlc_search, jlc_find_alternatives, jlc_stock_check, jlc_search_help.
Do NOT use any other tool to modify files except writing your one output JSON file. Do not edit KiCad files.

## Part 1 — DigiKey (keep the reel/TR numbers the designer already chose)
For each group:
1. If an existing dkpn ends in "-ND" (ignore trailing text like " - Cut Tape"): call digikey_get_part with that
   DigiKey number. If the returned mfr_part_number matches the group's mpn (case-insensitive, ignore spaces,
   "-", "/NOPB"-style suffix differences only if obviously the same part) -> status "ok", keep it unchanged.
   If it returns a different part or nothing -> status "wrong"; then look up the mpn (step 2) and propose that.
2. If dkpn is blank or not a DigiKey number (no "-ND"): call digikey_get_part with the mpn. Use the DigiKey
   number it returns -> status "filled" (note the old non-DigiKey value, e.g. an LCSC "C..." code or a Farnell number).
3. If DigiKey does not carry the mpn -> status "not_at_digikey" and explain.
Record for each: digikey_pn (final), digikey_stock, digikey_lifecycle (flag anything not "Active"), digikey_price.
DigiKey has a daily quota: at most ~2 calls per group. If you get a quota/rate error, stop calling DigiKey,
mark remaining groups "digikey_not_checked" and continue with JLC.

## Part 2 — JLCPCB / LCSC
For each group (including DNP ones, but say DNP in notes):
1. jlc_get_part(mpn=...) for the exact part.
2. PASSIVES (resistors, capacitors incl. electrolytic/polymer/tantalum, ferrite beads): if the exact part is at
   JLC as "basic" or "preferred" with stock >= needed qty -> use it ("exact"). Otherwise search for a
   Basic/Preferred equivalent (jlc_search with library_type="no_fee", package filter = same size) that meets ALL:
   - resistors: same resistance, same package size, tolerance equal or tighter, power rating >= original.
   - ceramic caps: same capacitance, same package size, voltage rating >= original, dielectric same or better
     (C0G/NP0 > X7R > X5R; never Y5V/Z5U), tolerance equal or tighter (for small C0G values in pF, tolerance in pF
     must be <= original where known).
   - electrolytic / polymer / tantalum caps: same technology (polymer stays polymer; aluminium electrolytic stays
     electrolytic), capacitance >= original, voltage >= original, same or smaller footprint that fits the same
     land pattern (same case size code), ESR <= original if the original specifies ESR.
   - ferrite beads: same package, impedance @100 MHz within +-25 %, rated current >= original, DCR <= original.
   If a qualifying Basic/Preferred part exists -> "substitute" (record its MPN, manufacturer, and the specs you
   compared). If none qualifies -> use the exact part even if "extended" ("exact_extended"); if the exact part is not
   at JLC either, pick the best qualifying extended equivalent ("substitute_extended").
3. EVERYTHING ELSE (ICs, transistors, LEDs, crystals/oscillators, inductors, connectors, switches, holders,
   mechanical): use the exact mpn at JLC if stocked ("exact" / "exact_extended"). Only if JLC does not carry it or
   has too little stock: look for a true drop-in (same footprint and pinout, same or better specs; e.g. a different
   packaging suffix of the same part, or a well-known second source). Record it as "candidate_needs_review" with a
   clear reason — do not present it as equivalent unless pin-out and key specs are confirmed from the tool data.
   If nothing suitable -> "not_at_jlc".
   Special care: oscillators must support the board supply voltage noted in the group notes; LED colours/sizes must
   match; connectors must be the same series/footprint.
4. Record: lcsc, jlc_mpn, jlc_manufacturer, library_type (basic/preferred/extended), jlc_stock, jlc_price,
   decision (exact / exact_extended / substitute / substitute_extended / candidate_needs_review / not_at_jlc),
   compared_specs (short string), notes.

## Output
Write ONE JSON file (path given in your task) containing a list with one object per input group:
{ "mpn", "refs", "value", "footprint",
  "digikey": {"status","existing","digikey_pn","stock","lifecycle","price","notes"},
  "jlc": {"decision","lcsc","jlc_mpn","jlc_manufacturer","library_type","stock","price","compared_specs","notes"} }
Then reply with a SHORT summary (<= 25 lines): counts per status/decision, and every group that is "wrong",
"not_at_digikey", "candidate_needs_review", "not_at_jlc", low stock, or non-Active lifecycle. Do not paste the JSON.
Be accurate: never invent part numbers; every number you record must come from a tool result.
